title: CJWasm2 Std Phase F Residual Failure Report

metadata.scope: scripts/std_test.sh L1 modules after Phases A-D

residual_clusters.summary: StringWriter UTF8 overloads and readback-to-string comparison are still not modeled end-to-end
representative_errors: CHIR 转换失败: invalid binary operator '!=' on type 'Int64' and 'String'
CHIR 转换失败: invalid binary operator '!=' on type 'String' and 'Int64'
likely_root_causes: StringWriter.write/writeln overload coverage is still compile-safe only, not type-accurate for scalar and string overload families
Static or constructor-style String conversion/readback paths such as String.fromUtf8(...) are still falling back to Int64 in some method-call shapes
Byte-array to String readback comparisons are not consistently typed as String on both sides
residual_clusters.recommended_next_action: Implement StringWriter overload typing plus String.fromUtf8/readback return typing, then re-run the whole StringWriter bucket.

residual_clusters.summary: ChainedInputStream still loses array-byte and stream-read semantics across read loops
representative_errors: CHIR 转换失败: mismatched types
CHIR 转换失败: invalid binary operator '!=' on type 'Int64' and 'Array<UInt8>'
likely_root_causes: Built-in nominal subtype relations such as File/FileReader/BufferedReader <: InputStream are not registered, so Array<InputStream> = [file1, file2, ...] still trips mismatched-types checks
ChainedInputStream constructor and read(Array<Byte>) contract are not modeled precisely enough
File.readFrom(...) and Array<Byte> equality/flow typing still fall back to Int64 in some chained stream paths
InputStream array element typing is likely incomplete in constructor/lowering paths
residual_clusters.recommended_next_action: Model ChainedInputStream(Array<InputStream>) and File.readFrom(...) as true byte-array paths, then re-check looped read/write chaining.

residual_clusters.summary: MultiOutputStream broadcast write semantics remain stubbed or mistyped
representative_errors: CHIR 转换失败: mismatched types
likely_root_causes: Built-in nominal subtype relations such as File/FileWriter/BufferedWriter <: OutputStream are not registered, so Array<OutputStream> = [file1, file2, ...] still fails before lowering
MultiOutputStream(Array<OutputStream>) constructor path is not modeled with the right container element semantics
write(Array<Byte>) and flush() on broadcast streams are still handled as opaque stubs, not as typed stream operations
OutputStream array element typing in for-in/constructor flows is still incomplete
residual_clusters.recommended_next_action: Add explicit MultiOutputStream pseudo-object semantics and align OutputStream-array constructor typing with the existing byte-stream model.

residual_clusters.summary: Console stdout float overloads are still mismatched
representative_errors: CHIR 转换失败: mismatched types
likely_root_causes: Console.stdOut.write/writeln currently lower to Print without normalizing float overloads to string output
Float16/Float32/Float64 console stream overloads are not being routed through the existing numeric-to-string machinery
residual_clusters.recommended_next_action: Route Console.stdOut.write(Float*) and writeln(Float*) through the same formatting path already used by print/println.

residual_clusters.summary: ioException is blocked by the explicit-main-return rule, not by stream semantics
representative_errors: CHIR 转换失败: main containing throw must declare an explicit return type
likely_root_causes: The main-function throw rule in src/chir/lower.rs is stricter than the std test expects for try/catch-contained throws
This is a semantic-policy issue rather than an io runtime gap
residual_clusters.recommended_next_action: Revisit the main throw restriction to allow fully handled throws in Unit-returning main, or explicitly classify this test as a policy mismatch.

proposed_tail_fix_batches.title: Close StringWriter and console write overload semantics
Add built-in stream subtype relations and close ChainedInputStream/MultiOutputStream typing
Resolve handled-throw policy mismatch in main

notes: Phase F currently converts the remaining non-macro compile failures into concrete work clusters.
WASM validation still has 16 failures among compile-passing std files; those are not yet decomposed in this first residual report.
The dominant next payoff remains io, not parser or generic conformance work.
scripts/std_test.sh currently names wasm outputs as mod + basename, which makes duplicate names under console/stdout and console/stderr hard to distinguish during diagnosis.
